info.title: Applicamp API
info.description: The Applicamp HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Operations either are public or take the web app's session cookie (`session`); unsafe methods also need the `X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and the app's own `Origin`.

get.description:
Every board, approved, waiting for the owner, paused or declined,
highest average salary first: the mean of the stated salaries of its
engineering jobs open to where the person lives (30 days), in euros a
year; a country-scoped board with fewer than 10 by its country's typical
pay; no salary data last. With the person's totals per board (7 and 30
days) and whether they manage the boards.

The person's searches and the discovery runs, newest first, ten a page,
each with what it scanned on every board: jobs read, passed their
requirements, scored by the AI, matched, the AI's cost, or why a board
was skipped (its polling limit) or failed; and what a discovery check
found. Filter by board or by search.

post.description:
Its site becomes a candidate, checked in the background (robots rules,
terms, a feed, a sample), and waits for the owner: nothing is read for
jobs before it is approved. At most 10 a day. The same site twice
answers the board already there (200).

200.description: That site is already a board.

202.description: Added as a candidate; the check runs.

get.description:
Its ranking, config, terms and the automatic check (robots rules, the
terms' sentences, sample jobs, the proposed attribution), and whether it
can be approved now.

post.description:
From then on searches read it. Only a candidate or a paused board with
no blocker: nothing the research found forbids reading it, its key is
set if it needs one, its config reads its kind, and its check (of the
feed's host) found robots rules that allow the feed. The problem names
the first blocker and says what exactly. Board owners only.

409.description: `not_waiting`: it is approved or declined; else its first blocker: `terms_forbid`, `robots_disallowed`, `needs_key`, `no_endpoint`, `config_invalid`, `check_needed`; the detail says what exactly

post.description:
Reads its robots rules (for its feed's host), terms page and a sample of
its jobs, once each, in the background; the board shows the result.
Board owners only.

202.description: The check runs in the background.

put.description:
The whole config, validated for the board's kind (or the new `kind`, as
a check's proposal gives it); unknown keys refused; a problem names the
field. An approved board's new feed must still be allowed by the robots
rules its check found. The seed list never overwrites it again. Board
owners only.

400.description: `invalid_config`: the detail names the field and says what is wrong

409.description: `robots_disallowed`: an approved board's new feed is not allowed by its robots rules; `kind_locked`: an approved board keeps its kind

post.description: It is never read, and says why. Board owners only.

put.summary: Set a job board's API key.
put.description:
One value per parameter its config's `key` names, each 1 to 200 visible
characters. Stored sealed with the instance secret and sent only to the
host its config reads now; never returned (the board says "key set").
Board owners only.

409.description: `no_key_needed`: its config names no key; `no_endpoint`: it has no address to send it to

delete.summary: Remove a job board's API key.
delete.description: Searches stop reading it until a key is set again. Board owners only.

post.description: Searches stop reading it until it is approved again. Board owners only.

get.description:
The PDF versions and the drafts still being reviewed, across all the
opportunities of the account (the ones put away included: a PDF is what was
sent), newest first. Never calls a model.
Version 0 and no answers until they answer a question.

put.description:
All the answers at once, as the interview or an edit leaves them; a
question left out is unanswered. Values are trimmed and blank ones
removed. Lists over their limit (5 roles; 10 places, things to avoid and
must-haves), a currency that is not ISO 4217 or a choice that does not
exist are refused. Every save, even of the same answers, is a new version.

200.description: The goals, saved, at their new version.

get.description:
The account behind the session cookie, with the providers linked to it.
Never a token.

Every opportunity of the signed-in person, newest first, except the
dismissed ones ("Not for me") and the hidden ones (they fail a hard
requirement; `hidden=true` lists only those, with the reason). Filter by
stage, by text in the role, company or place, or to the new ones.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only those whose role, company or place contains this.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: Only the new ones (Found, never opened).

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description:
Only the hidden ones: found before the requirement rules, they fail
one. Left out otherwise.

post.summary: Add a job by its link.
post.description:
A Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby posting is read from the board's public API
(title, company, place, pay, description), and that company's board is
searched from then on. Any other link becomes an opportunity with the
link and the title and company given (typed later if not): the server
never fetches it. The same posting twice answers the one already there
(200).

200.description: That posting was already in the pipeline.

get.description:
One of the signed-in person's, dismissed ones included. Anyone else's is
not found.

patch.description:
Its stage, next step, notes, "Not for me" (`dismissed`), or that it was
opened (no longer new). Title, company and place can be typed only for
one added by a link to a site that is not a job board.

409.description: `not_editable`: its title, company and place come from the job board

get.description:
What a tailored CV for it would be based on, as it is now: the company's
site (or that the person has to type it), the facts read on it, what the
job wants most, the questions where the profile is thin, what each step
costs and what was spent. **Never calls the model and never fetches.**
Another account's opportunity is not found.

delete.description: It stays removed on later reads, and Undo (`…/restore`) brings it back.

post.summary: Undo a removal: the fact is back.

post.description:
**One small model call** reads the answer as Grill me does, with the same
checks: each fact quotes the person's own words and says nothing they or
their profile do not. The facts wait on the position the question is about
(the most recent one when it names none: `defaulted`), to be kept, fixed or
dropped with Grill me's endpoints (`/api/v1/profile/grill/proposals/{id}/…`).
Nothing reaches the profile until a click.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

post.description:
For a question about a skill: the skill is recorded as not theirs (like a
dismissed suggestion), and neither it nor this question is asked about
again. No model call. A question with no skill is a 400.

400.description: `no_skill`: the question is not about a skill

post.summary: Skip a question: it is hidden for this opportunity. No model call.
Read about the company and compare the job.
post.description:
Reads the company's own pages (the posting, its home page and up to five
pages it links to about the company; the same site only, where robots.txt
allows) and makes the facts: **one model call**, reused for 30 days per
company unless `again=true`. Then compares the posting with those facts and
a compact profile: **one more call**, reused until the posting changes.
Each fact must quote the page it cites, or it is left out. At most
20 company reads per account per UTC day, fetches included.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

parameters.name: again
parameters.description: Read the company's pages again, even though its facts are fresh.

put.description:
Only its host (and port) is kept, on the company: it is asked once, and
wins over every guess. The address must be one the server may ask (a public
https address). A different site than before forgets the facts read on the
old one.

get.summary: The tailored CV of an opportunity.
get.description:
The latest draft with each line's sources, marks and reasons, what was
left out, the job's keywords against it, the approved versions, the caps
and the spend. **Never calls the model.** Another account's opportunity is
not found.

post.summary: Draft a CV for this job.
post.description:
**One model call.** From the posting, what the job wants, the company
facts not removed and the profile; each line cites the profile sources it
comes from, and the server then checks that it says nothing they do not.
The model never sees a name or contact details. Needs the opportunity at
Shortlisted or later. At most 10 drafts per opportunity and 20 per account
per UTC day; nothing retries past a limit. A new draft puts the earlier
unapproved one away.

200.description: The CV, with the new draft.

post.description:
Refused (409 `lines_flagged`) while any line or skill cannot be traced to
the profile. The draft is frozen, its text rendered as a PDF with the
`template` and `length` asked for (Clean, 1 page by default), the PDF read
back out and compared with the CV, and the PDF kept as the next version:
all or nothing. If it does not fit the length (`cv_doesnt_fit`) or the
read-back finds it lacking (`cv_pdf_check_failed`, with the reasons, one
per line), nothing is approved. Contact details are read from the profile
again. No model call.

requestBody.description: The look of the PDF; optional.

post.description: An approved version cannot be discarded. No model call.

patch.summary: Change one line of a draft.
patch.description:
`{text}` edits it: the new text is checked against the **same sources**
(an edited line that is not a summary drops its company-fact citations).
`{remove: true}` removes the line (a position left with no line goes to
"left out"), or the skill. No model call. Only a draft can change.

404.description: `not_found`: no such opportunity, draft or line

post.summary: "It's true: add it to my profile."
post.description:
The person's own words become a fact kept on the line's position (its
`quote` is the text; `area` defaults to `results`), as Grill me's Keep
does, and the line is checked again with that fact as an extra source.
For a skill it adds the skill to the profile instead. A summary or
headline puts the fact on the most recent position. No model call.

200.description: The CV, after the line was checked again.

post.summary: Put back what the draft left out, as the profile has it.
post.description:
`{position}` puts a position left out back with up to three of its lines
(highlights, else kept facts, else its summary), word for word; `{source}`
puts one left-out line back on its position. Each cites its own source, so
it passes the check. No model call.

200.description: The CV, with it put back.

404.description: `not_found`: no such draft, position or line

post.summary: Make another version of the approved CV.
post.description:
The latest approved draft's text, rendered with `template` and `length`
(what the newest version has when left out), read back, and kept as the
next version. **No model call.** The earlier versions are untouched. Refused
when the text does not fit the length (`cv_doesnt_fit`) or the read-back
finds the PDF lacking (`cv_pdf_check_failed`, with the reasons, one per
line). At most 20 versions per opportunity.

200.description: The CV, with the new version.

get.description:
`Content-Type: application/pdf`, shown inline, named
`<Name> CV - <Company>.pdf`. `?download=1` serves it as an attachment and
sets the version's `downloaded_at`. Never cached, never sniffed. Another
account's version is not found.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `1` serves it as an attachment and records the download.

get.description: Empty (and no `source`) until they import or write one.

put.description:
The whole profile, as edited by hand. Values are trimmed and empty ones
removed; a value over its length, a date not like `2020`, `2020-03` or
`2020-03-15`, or a list of more than 200 entries is refused.

post.description:
The profile is unchanged. Discarding twice is fine; a kept draft cannot
be discarded.

Writes it into the profile as a new profile version whose source is
`answer`, and marks the question done. `items` may be edited first.
Refused with 409 `profile_changed` when the profile changed since the
draft was made.

get.summary: Every position with how far its interview is.
get.description: Computed from the stored interviews; never calls the model.

post.summary: Drop a fact: it is not kept and not shown again.

200.description: The interview, after the fact was dropped.

404.description: `not_found`: no such fact, or it expired

post.summary: Keep a fact, as it is or fixed.
post.description:
Writes it on the position in the profile as a new profile version. A
fixed `text` is checked like the model's: it may say only what the quote
or the profile says (400 `fact_not_supported` names the words that are
not there); the quote never changes.

200.description: The interview, after the fact was kept.

404.description: `not_found`: no such fact, or it expired

get.summary:
The interview of one position: its turns, coverage, the facts waiting and
the question waiting for an answer. Never calls the model.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

post.description:
**One model call** reads the answer: it returns the facts the answer
states (each with the person's exact words), what it covered and the next
question, which pushes back when the answer was vague. A fact whose quote
is not in the answer, or that says a number, name or tool neither the
quote nor the profile says, is left out and counted in the turn's
`dropped`. Nothing reaches the profile until a fact is kept.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

404.description: `not_found`: no such position, or not started

post.summary:
End the interview for now. No model call; the question waiting is put
away, and starting again makes a new one. Facts waiting stay for their
24 hours.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

404.description: `not_found`: no such position, or not started

post.summary: Keep every fact waiting on a position, as they are. One profile version.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

200.description: The interview, after the facts were kept.

post.description:
Its area is left alone until the interview is started again, and the
next question is made: **one model call**, or none when nothing is left
to ask.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

404.description: `not_found`: no such position, or not started

post.summary: Start (or take up) the interview of a position.
post.description:
With a question waiting, that one is shown again and the model is not
called. Otherwise this is **one model call** that makes the next question.
Areas skipped before are asked about again.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The position's place in the profile's `work` list.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `pt-PT`; English when left out.

post.description:
A `multipart/form-data` upload of `kind` and either `file` (a LinkedIn
export ZIP, up to 20 MB; a PDF, up to 8 MB) or `text` (up to 60 000
characters). The answer is a draft to review: the profile is unchanged
until the draft is applied. The file is not kept.

A ZIP is read from its CSVs without any model; it is refused before
anything is extracted when it holds more than 200 files, a file over
5 MB or more than 50 MB uncompressed, or a path leaving the archive.
A PDF's text and pasted text are structured by the `complete` model, and
every value the source does not say is dropped and counted (`dropped`).

503.description: `ai_unavailable`: no model to read a PDF or text (import the LinkedIn ZIP instead); `ai_daily_limit_reached`; `ai_failed`

get.description:
One of the signed-in person's imports, until it expires. Anyone else's
is not found.

post.description:
`replace` makes the draft the profile; `merge` keeps the profile as it
is (hand edits included) and adds what the draft has that it does not.
Once applied, a draft cannot be applied again.

The profile is unchanged. Discarding twice is fine; an applied draft
cannot be discarded.

get.summary: The questions that would make the profile stronger.
get.description:
The first request for a profile and goals version starts the AI review in
the background (one model call) and answers 202 `running`; ask again in a
moment. The review is kept until the profile or goals change by any other
way than the person's own kept answers. Without a model, or over a
spending limit, the status says so (`unavailable`, `failed`) and the
checklist from `GET /api/v1/profile/strength` still works.

200.description: The questions (or why there are none).

post.summary: Try the review again after it failed.
post.description:
Only a failed review is started again, and the spending limits still
apply: over one, it fails again at once without calling the model.

200.description: The questions (or why there are none).

post.summary: Make a draft from an answer.
post.description:
One small model call. The draft may say only what the answer or the
profile says: a line with a number, a name or a tool that neither
contains is left out and counted in `dropped`. Nothing is saved until the
draft is kept. Asking again for the same question replaces the draft.
It is not asked again for this version of the profile.

put.summary: Put the skills in a new order.
put.description:
The first three skills drive the job board searches. `names` must be
the profile's skills exactly, each once; nothing is added or removed.

200.description: The profile, with its skills in order.

get.description:
Skills that the person's own position descriptions mention but their
skills list does not, with the number of positions each is in. Each
name is checked against the text of the positions (whole words), so
nothing is suggested that the profile does not say. Uses the same
review as the questions; 202 while it runs.

post.summary: Add a suggested skill to the profile.
post.description: It goes at the end of the skills, in the order the person adds them.

post.summary: Say a suggested skill is not theirs.
post.description: It is not suggested again, whatever the profile says later.

get.summary: The strength of the signed-in person's profile.
get.description:
Computed from the profile and goals, never by a model. Each part that is
not full says what to do about it. Reading it never starts a review.

post.description:
Reads the job boards, keeps the jobs within the goals' hard limits,
scores the best 40 against the profile and goals, and adds the good
matches as Found; follow it with `GET /api/v1/searches/latest`. At most
3 a day and one every 15 minutes (the instance may set others), never
past the spending limits.

202.description: Started; it runs in the background.

409.description: `profile_needed`: set up the profile and answer a goals question first; `search_running`: one is already running

429.description: `search_limit_reached`: the detail says when to try again

503.description: `ai_unavailable`: no model is set up; `ai_budget_reached`: a spending limit is reached

get.summary: About what a search would cost.
get.description:
The jobs it would likely score (the last search's, at most 40), times
what a batch of ten has cost this person on average, in euros; and what
they spent today and this month against their limits. Over €0.05 the
app asks before searching.

The signed-in person's newest search, running or done: how many jobs it
read, kept, scored and added, why it stopped if it did, and its cost.

How far the signed-in person is with their profile and goals, how many
new matches wait for them, their latest search, and the next step.

Checks `state` against the login cookie, redeems the code, validates the
ID token, and signs the person in if their provider identity is linked
or their verified address is on the invite list: a session cookie and a
redirect to `/`. Someone not on the list lands on `/not-invited`; any
failure on `/sign-in?error=sign_in_failed`. The login cookie is cleared
either way.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` sent with the authorization request.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: An error code instead of a code.

303.description: To `/` signed in (with the session cookie), to `/not-invited`, or to `/sign-in?error=sign_in_failed`.

get.description: Only the configured ones; the sign-in page shows one button each.

get.summary: Start signing in with a provider.
get.description:
Seals a new sign-in (`state`, `nonce`, PKCE verifier) into a
ten-minute, `SameSite=Lax` login cookie and redirects to the provider's
authorization endpoint.

303.description: To the provider, or to `/sign-in?error=provider_unavailable` when it cannot be reached.

post.description:
Deletes the session on the server and clears the cookie. Needs the
`X-Applicamp-CSRF: 1` header and a same-origin request, like every
unsafe request.

204.description: Signed out (also when there was no session).

get.description: `ok` when the server answers and reaches its database.

AnswerProposal.description: A fact taken from an answer, waiting for Keep, Fix or Drop.

area.description: What it is about (Grill me's areas).

text.description: In their own words, 1 to 2000 characters.

defaulted.description: The question named no position, so the most recent one was used.

proposals.description: The facts, checked against the person's words and the profile.

role.description: The position the facts are about.

mode.description: Replace the profile, or merge into it.

ApplyMode.description: How a draft reaches the profile.

Area.description:
What a fact about a position is about: the seven things "Grill me" goes
through, in order.

Autonomy.description:
How much agents may do alone. Applying and emailing always wait for the
person, whatever this says.

location.description: Where they are, as written ("Lisbon, Portugal").

Blocked.description: Why a draft cannot be made now.

BoardBlocker.description: Why a board cannot be approved yet.

code.description:
`terms_forbid`, `robots_disallowed`, `needs_key`, `no_endpoint`,
`config_invalid`, `check_needed`; clients translate the ones they
know and show `detail` for any other.

detail.description: What exactly, in English: the terms' sentence, the rule, the field.

source.description: Where it says so (the terms page, robots.txt).

config.description: The whole config, validated for the board's kind.

oneOf.description:
A new kind for it (a proposal that found a feed on an API board);
its kind stays when left out.

BoardDetail.description: A job board, whole: its check, config and terms.

approvable.description: It can be approved now; else `blockers` say why.

blocked.description:
The first blocker's code (`terms_forbid`, `robots_disallowed`,
`needs_key`, `no_endpoint`, `config_invalid`, `check_needed`), or
none.

blockers.description:
Everything that stands between the board and its approval, in order,
each with its detail; empty when it can be approved.

config.description: How it is read (the config's JSON).

endpoint.description: The address its jobs are read from.

oneOf.description:
The API key its config says it needs: how to get one, and whether it
is set. Never the key.
What the automatic check found; none before it ran.

BoardKey.description: A board's API key, as a client sees it: never the key itself.

params.description: The parameters it is sent in (one field each).

set.description: A key is set for the host its config reads.

BoardKeyChange.description: A board's API key: one value per parameter its config names.

BoardList.description: The job boards, highest average salary first (none last).

can_manage.description: The signed-in person manages the boards.

BoardPriority.description: How much a board matters to a remote search.

BoardProposal.description: A config a check proposes, and the kind it reads.

config.description: The config's JSON, as `PUT …/config` takes it.

BoardRanking.description: A board's average salary and its key in the order.

avg_salary_eur_year.description: The mean of its relevant jobs' stated salaries, in euros a year.

oneOf.description: The country benchmark it ranks by, when it does.

key.description: What it is sorted by, in euros a year; none sorts last.

relevant_jobs.description: Relevant jobs (engineering, open to where the person lives, 30 days).

salaried_jobs.description: Relevant jobs that state a salary.

BoardReport.description:
What the automatic check found. Every sentence and job in it is copied
from the board's site: data, never instructions.

attribution.description: How the app would credit it.

config_fingerprint.description:
A fingerprint of the config the check read with: a seeded board
whose config changed since is checked again at start.

flags.description:
What the owner should know ("robots.txt disallows the API",
"terms changed since approval").

oneOf.description: A feed found (`rss`), or an API (`json_api`), or `jsonld_sitemap`.

notes.description: For the owner, in a sentence (the seed list's notes).

oneOf.description:
A config the check found for a board without a usable one: the
owner may use it ("Use this config"); never applied by itself to a
seeded or edited board.

remote_share.description: Share of the sample that is remote (0–1).

sample.description: Up to 20 jobs parsed with the proposed config.

terms_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the terms page, to notice a change.

terms_sentences.description:
Its sentences about scraping, robots, automation, aggregation, the
API, linking back, attribution or commercial use, verbatim (at most
10).

worldwide_share.description: Share of the sample open worldwide (0–1).

BoardStatus.description: Where a board stands with the owner.

BoardSummary.description: A job board, as the Boards page lists it.

attribution.description: How its jobs are credited ("From Himalayas").

country.description: The one country its jobs are in, when it is country-scoped.

flags.description: What the owner should know (from its check).

last_error.description: What went wrong at its last fetch.

note.description: Its check's note, for a candidate.

priority.description: A label only: the order is the salary ranking.

ranking.description: Its average salary and its key in the order.

oneOf.description:
How well its jobs fit the person's top skills; none without skills
or listed jobs.

slug.description: Its stable name: the source its jobs carry.

totals_7d.description: The person's searches on it over the last 7 days.

BoardTerms.description: What a board's terms ask, and where they say it.

apply_unchanged.description: The apply link is used as the board gives it.

drop_expired.description: Jobs past their expiry are taken out of view.

link_back.description: A link back to the posting on the board is required.

max_fetches_per_day.description: Fetches a day, at most (its polling interval keeps to it).

no_redistribution.description: Its jobs are never republished elsewhere.

notes.description: What else matters, in a sentence or two.

BoardTotals.description: What a board did for the person over some days.

cost_eur.description: What the AI cost on its jobs, in euros.

company.description: The company, as the opportunity names it.

facts.description: The facts, removed ones included (marked), oldest first.

oneOf.description:
The most recent position of the profile: where an answer goes when
its question names none.

questions.description: The questions, in the order they are asked.

oneOf.description: The last read; none until the company was read.

site.description: Its website (an origin); none until it is known.

site_needed.description: The person has to type the site (once).

wants.description: What the job wants most; none until it was compared.

BriefFact.description: A fact read on the company's own site.

quote.description: The page's own words that say it.

removed.description: The person removed it ("Wrong, remove"); Undo restores it.

url.description: The page it was read on.

BriefQuestion.description: A question where the profile is thin for what the job wants.

oneOf.description:
The position an answer is about; none: the most recent one
(`latest_role` of the brief) and the page says so.

question.description: It names the company fact or the posting line it comes from.

skill.description:
The skill it is about, if it is about one: "I don't have it" is
offered.

BriefSpend.description: What was spent, and the cap on company reads.

reads_cap.description: The most company reads an account can start in a UTC day.

BriefWant.description: Something the job wants, with the posting's words.

level.description: `must` when the posting requires it, `nice` when it only prefers it.

quote.description: The posting's exact words for it.

CashFloor.description: The least they would take, before tax.

CompanyRead.description: The last read of the company's pages.

facts_dropped.description: Facts left out because their quote is not on the page they cite.
